note: Maps every D1-D8 equivalence dimension to the artifacts that carry it. Executable engine cases live in generation-scoped-json-conformance.json and run against the pinned engine. Compiler-boundary dimensions are carried by named unit tests, because the construct they exclude cannot be expressed in the IIR and so has no row form. ClickHouse status is not_claimed under PostgreSQL activation per the ADR-0004 amendment of 2026-09-15; it becomes claimed only with its own evidence and a second independent review.

dimensions.title: null and missing
dimensions.postgresql_enforcement: The statement's decode guard refuses a missing or JSON-null group key or measure with SQLSTATE 22P02 before grouping, so no NULL group or NULL sum can be produced.

dimensions.title: precision and range
divergence_motivated_exclusions: decimal_excess_scale stays inadmissible. PostgreSQL's decode guard now refuses it outright; without the guard PostgreSQL would round it where ClickHouse truncates. The exclusion survives single-engine activation so ClickHouse can join the rule later without renegotiating it.
dimensions.postgresql_enforcement: The decode guard admits only canonical Decimal(38,9) text, so excess scale and values of 10^29 or more are refused with 22P02 instead of being rounded or reaching a cast; finite Decimal(57,9) overflow is refused by the result cast with 22003.

dimensions.title: collation
dimensions.negative_not_applicable_reason: Group strings use profile-specific binary semantics, so every distinct byte sequence is a distinct group and no input is inadmissible on collation grounds. Provider sort order differs for case variants, so result ordering is not claimed and the positive cases assert an equivalent row set rather than an equivalent row sequence.
dimensions.postgresql_enforcement: The statement groups the decoded string under an explicit COLLATE "C", recorded on the result column in the live evidence, so grouping is bytewise regardless of the database's default collation.

dimensions.title: locale
dimensions.negative_not_applicable_reason: The IIR can express the case-conversion functions lower and upper, so the locale claim rests on the restricted shape predicate rather than the IIR vocabulary. A case conversion is not a direct declared source input, so the projection check rejects it before emission and it has no row form.

dimensions.title: timezone
dimensions.negative_not_applicable_reason: The IIR can declare timestamp columns and datetime literals, so the timezone claim rests on the restricted shape predicate. Grouping admits only non-null string columns and the measure admits only a non-null decimal column, so no timestamp expression survives to emission. Evaluation time is separately required to be UTC.

dimensions.title: identifier encoding
dimensions.negative_not_applicable_reason: Identifier encoding is rejected at the compiler boundary before any statement is emitted, so an inadmissible identifier never reaches the engine and has no row form.

dimensions.title: literal typing
divergence_motivated_exclusions: wrong_type_decimal stays inadmissible. PostgreSQL's decode guard refuses a JSON number; ClickHouse, which has no guard, still coerces it. The exclusion is a contract requirement, not a PostgreSQL limitation, and survives single-engine activation.
dimensions.postgresql_enforcement: The decode guard requires every landing field to be a JSON string and the decimal field to match the canonical pattern; JSON numbers, booleans, arrays, objects, NaN, Infinity, hex, underscores, exponents, whitespace, signs and leading zeros are refused with 22P02.

dimensions.title: relational behavior
dimensions.negative_not_applicable_reason: Joins, filters, deduplication, ordering, limits, and additional measures are excluded by the shape predicate before emission, so they have no row form. Their rejection is carried by the shape tests below.
